question: A researcher wants to see if a new handwashing technique cuts down ward infections better than the old one. What is the best approach?

options.A: Guessing the outcome based on personal feelings
options.B: Asking the oldest nurse on the ward for advice
options.C: Following whatever tradition feels most comfortable
options.D: The scientific method using a structured trial

explanation: Testing a clear idea with structured observation is the true hallmark of the scientific method in action.

question: Which of these tiny germs cannot survive on its own and must enter a living host cell to multiply?

options.A: A virus
options.B: A bacterium
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A parasite

explanation: Viruses are tiny! They lack the internal machinery to reproduce by themselves, so they have to hijack a living host cell to make copies. You've got this!

question: An increasing population of older adults in Nigeria will most likely lead to a higher demand for what service?

options.A: Management of chronic health conditions
options.B: Primary school infrastructure
options.C: Pediatric immunizations and infant care
options.D: Obstetric and maternity wards

explanation: Older populations experience higher rates of long-term illnesses like high blood pressure and diabetes, increasing the need for chronic care. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main underlying cause of osteoarthritis?

options.A: An autoimmune attack on the joint lining
options.B: A sudden bacterial infection in the bone marrow
options.C: Wear and tear breakdown of joint cartilage over time
options.D: A total lack of synovial fluid from birth

explanation: You got it! Osteoarthritis is primarily a degenerative condition where the protective cartilage cushions wear down over the years.

question: Which of the following is NOT a nurse's role in community Family Life Education?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations in schools
options.B: Acting as an advocate for adolescent health
options.C: Serving as an educator for health promotion
options.D: Counseling families on resource availability

explanation: Nurses do not do surgeries in schools! Our focus is on health education, counseling, and supporting our clients.

question: How do modern nutritional guidelines differ from the ones created in the early 20th century?

options.A: They now focus on preventing chronic diseases in addition to stopping deficiencies
options.B: They have completely removed any guidelines regarding vitamins and minerals
options.C: They only focus on calculating the exact amount of daily calories needed
options.D: They are designed exclusively for treating severe hospital patients

explanation: You got it! While older guidelines just wanted to stop diseases like rickets, today we also look at long-term wellness, like preventing heart disease and obesity.

question: In the female reproductive system, where does fertilization usually take place?

options.A: Fallopian tube
options.B: Uterine cavity
options.C: Ovarian surface
options.D: Vaginal canal

explanation: The fallopian tube is where the magic happens! It is the pathway where a sperm meets and fertilizes the egg.

question: What is a major feature of employer-sponsored health insurance?

options.A: It forbids patients from seeing private medical doctors
options.B: It is completely managed by the Ministry of Health
options.C: It is strictly limited to retired civil servants
options.D: It is provided by companies as part of worker compensation

explanation: Spot on! Employer-sponsored plans are job benefits where companies help cover or fully pay health insurance for their staff.

question: What defines a pre-testicular cause of male infertility?

options.A: A physical blockage within the epididymis preventing sperm release
options.B: A genetic mutation residing directly on the chromosomes inside the sperm
options.C: A hormonal or systemic problem outside the testes that disrupts sperm production
options.D: An infection of the prostate gland that damages the seminal fluid

explanation: Pre-testicular issues originate in the brain or endocrine system before the signal ever reaches the testicles. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h2)

question: What is the specific, go-to antidote for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Flumazenil
options.D: Acetylcysteine

explanation: You'll see this often in the ward! Acetylcysteine saves the liver by restocking its natural protector (glutathione) just in time before paracetamol metabolites cause damage.

question: What is the main point of health planning in a community?

options.A: Identifying health problems and using resources to meet goals
options.B: Reducing the total number of patients admitted to wards
options.C: Building more private hospitals in urban centers
options.D: Increasing the salary of medical and nursing personnel

explanation: You've got this! Health planning is simply finding out what health issues a community faces and figuring out how to use available resources to solve them.

question: What is the main purpose of the Child Rights Act passed in Nigeria in 2003?

options.A: Setting retirement ages for civil servants
options.B: Managing federal highway construction
options.C: Legal protection for child survival, development, and protection
options.D: Regulating international trade tariffs

explanation: The Child Rights Act domesticates international laws to ensure every Nigerian child is legally protected from abuse, neglect, and exploitation.

question: A man and a woman of the same weight each have two standard drinks. What is the most likely result?

options.A: The male patient will absorb the alcohol much faster than the female patient
options.B: Neither patient will absorb any alcohol into their systemic circulation
options.C: The female patient will have a noticeably higher blood alcohol concentration
options.D: Both patients will have the exact same blood alcohol concentration

explanation: Body composition matters! Differences in body water and metabolism mean women generally hit higher blood alcohol levels than men from the exact same drink.

question: Which of these is a modern, digital way to share nursing research?

options.A: Paper memos locked inside a supervisor desk drawer
options.B: Locked institutional archives in university basements
options.C: Professional social media networks and infographics
options.D: Printed textbooks published twenty years ago

explanation: Exactly! Digital tools like social media and colorful infographics help spread useful health tips quickly to a wide audience.

question: Why do surgeons sometimes place antibiotic beads right inside a bone cavity after cleaning it out?

options.A: To stimulate rapid hair growth around the surgical incision
options.B: To act as permanent replacement for missing bone mineral
options.C: To permanently block blood flow and prevent further swelling
options.D: To deliver high concentrations of medication directly to the infected site

explanation: Those little beads release a high dose of medicine right where it's needed most, straight into the bone pocket while keeping the rest of the body safe.

question: What does 'medication reconciliation' mean in home health care?

options.A: Comparing current prescribed drugs with what the patient actually takes
options.B: Disposing of all expired prescription drugs found in the bathroom
options.C: Ordering new medication supplies directly from the local pharmacy
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of monthly prescription refills

explanation: You got it! Medication reconciliation is just checking what the doctor wrote against what the patient is actually swallowing (plus any local herbs or supplements!). Keeps everyone safe.

question: What is an 'outlier' on a scatter diagram?

options.A: A data point located far away from the main pattern
options.B: The average score calculated for the entire group
options.C: The very first dot plotted on the bottom left corner
options.D: A label written incorrectly on the vertical axis

explanation: An outlier is just a rebel dot that sits far away from everyone else's general trend. You'll spot them easily!

question: Why is it important to teach family members how to spot early warning signs?

options.A: Family members are qualified to prescribe psychiatric drugs
options.B: It removes all responsibility from the healthcare team
options.C: It ensures the family pays for all clinic supplies
options.D: Family members live with the patient and can spot changes early

explanation: Because relatives spend the most time with the patient at home, they are often the first to notice when behavior starts changing. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which residential model features 24-hour staff presence for high support?

options.A: Self-contained private flats
options.B: Supervised hostels
options.C: Temporary weekend shelters
options.D: Transitional living facilities

explanation: Well done! Supervised hostels have staff around the clock to give extra guidance to residents who still need help with daily routines and medications.

question: What does your body do with extra carbohydrates when you eat more than you immediately need?

options.A: It converts all excess carbohydrates directly into bone tissue.
options.B: It eliminates them completely through the urinary system.
options.C: It stores the extra fuel as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
options.D: It turns them into water molecules to hydrate the cells.

explanation: Nothing goes to waste! When you have extra energy, your body packs it away neatly as glycogen in your liver and muscles for later use.

question: What causes pregnant women to frequently experience constipation and heartburn?

options.A: Expectant mothers consume too much iron too early in the first trimester.
options.B: Increased stomach acid burns away the lining of the small intestine.
options.C: High levels of progesterone slow down smooth muscle movement in the gut.
options.D: The expanding uterus completely shuts down all digestive enzyme production.

explanation: Blame progesterone! This pregnancy hormone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body, which slows down digestion and causes sluggish bowels and acid reflux.

question: What does a conceptual framework mainly display?

options.A: The exact daily schedule of the researcher
options.B: Patient room numbers in a hospital ward
options.C: Key factors and their presumed relationships
options.D: The monetary cost of nursing equipment

explanation: It's like a picture of your thoughts: it shows the main variables you are studying and how you expect them to influence each other.

question: Which of these is NOT a correct infection control step when nursing a patient with active TB?

options.A: Ensuring nurses wear fitted N95 respirator masks
options.B: Placing the patient in an airborne infection isolation room
options.C: Instructing the patient to cover their mouth when coughing
options.D: Keeping the patient's room doors and windows tightly sealed shut from fresh air

explanation: Sealing a room shut traps the infectious germs inside! We always need good ventilation or negative pressure to clear out the air safely.

question: Which arteries run straight down the center of the corpora cavernosa?

options.A: Internal iliac arteries
options.B: Bulbourethral arteries
options.C: Dorsal penile arteries
options.D: Cavernous arteries

explanation: Spot on! The cavernous arteries travel right through the middle, pumping blood straight into the tiny spaces inside.

question: Why is nurse-led advocacy essential for the prevention of mental health disorders?

options.A: Nurses can influence public policy and secure funding for community prevention programs
options.B: Nurses have the legal authority to pass national laws without legislative voting
options.C: Lawmakers only listen to nurses and ignore all other healthcare professionals
options.D: Advocacy replaces the need for direct clinical care in hospitals

explanation: Nurses use their frontline experience and health data to convince leaders to invest resources into preventive mental health initiatives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h8)

question: How does prolonged bed rest and immobility most directly harm the cardiovascular and skin systems?

options.A: It lowers the body temperature to dangerous levels.
options.B: It promotes blood clots in deep veins and breaks down skin integrity.
options.C: It immediately stops the kidneys from producing urine.
options.D: It causes the patient to drink too much water.

explanation: When blood pools from lack of movement, clots form easily, and constant pressure on skin leads to painful, hard-to-heal pressure ulcers. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h2)

question: How does the vagus nerve normally affect the heart rate?

options.A: It stops ventricular contraction completely
options.B: It speeds up the heart rate
options.C: It slows down the heart rate
options.D: It strengthens the force of atrial contraction only

explanation: The vagus nerve is part of your body's 'rest and digest' system. When it acts on the heart, it helps calm things down and slows the heart rate.

question: What is the best way to start counselling a mother whose child is experiencing growth faltering?

options.A: Tell the mother to stop coming to the clinic until next year
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about recent feeding and illness
options.C: Scold the mother for failing to feed the child properly
options.D: Write a prescription for expensive imported vitamin supplements

explanation: Great nursing starts with empathy and listening. Ask gentle, open questions to understand what's happening at home without judging.

question: In family planning care, what does 'compliance' mean?

options.A: Whether the clinic follows national healthcare budgeting guidelines
options.B: Whether the partner agrees with the choice of contraceptive
options.C: Whether the manufacturer tests the product for chemical safety
options.D: Whether the client follows the precise instructions for using the method

explanation: Compliance simply means how well and accurately a client sticks to the correct usage guidelines for their birth control.

question: Why are gentle range-of-motion exercises and turning schedules crucial for residents who cannot move much on their own?

options.A: To speed up the metabolic rate and cure underlying chronic infections
options.B: To prevent secondary complications like contractures and pressure injuries
options.C: To eliminate the need for any nutritional support or dietary supplements
options.D: To guarantee that the resident will never need assistance walking again

explanation: Moving and turning patients keeps their joints flexible and protects their skin from painful pressure sores. Excellent nursing practice!

question: According to Rubin's maternal role theory, what is the first major task an expectant mother focuses on?

options.A: Ensuring safe passage for herself and her child
options.B: Rejection of her own childhood parenting style
options.C: Immediate financial planning for college
options.D: Complete isolation from social networks

explanation: Spot on. Keeping herself and the baby safe and healthy is always the number one early priority for an expectant mum.

question: Why do safe motherhood programs pay close attention to maternal morbidity alongside mortality?

options.A: To prevent long-term suffering and disability in women who survive
options.B: Because pregnancy illnesses are much easier to treat than pregnancy deaths
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of operating maternity wards
options.D: To ensure accurate record keeping for government health insurance

explanation: Looking at morbidity helps us protect and restore the quality of life for mothers who make it through tough complications. Every survivor deserves full healing!

question: What is the primary job of cytotoxic T cells?

options.A: To form the physical skin barrier against outside bacteria
options.B: To slow down the immune response once an infection clears
options.C: To produce massive quantities of free-floating antibodies
options.D: To destroy virus-infected or abnormal body cells directly

explanation: Cytotoxic T cells are the hit squad—they sniff out and destroy body cells that have been hijacked by viruses or turned cancerous.

question: A patient on face mask oxygen suddenly drops in saturation and the tubing feels warm and static. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Normal adjustment of the lungs to high flow rates

question: During which step of the nursing process do standardized care plans and pathways guide your choices the most?

options.C: Assessment
options.D: Planning

question: Which health problem is most directly linked to poverty and poor sanitation in developing regions?

options.A: Genetic blood disorders
options.B: Traumatic bone fractures
options.C: Type 1 Diabetes mellitus
options.D: Cholera and malaria

question: Why do the ureters enter the bladder wall at a slant (oblique angle)?

options.C: To shorten the overall length of the lower ureter tract

question: What is the first thing a nurse should review before going on a home visit?

options.A: The client's past medical and psychiatric records

options.C: The personal phone numbers of the client's neighbors
options.D: The transport fare prices in the local market

question: You are the first nurse to arrive at an accident scene and you notice a strong smell of leaking gas. What is your very first step?

options.A: Wait inside the ambulance until police complete all paperwork.
options.B: Run immediately to pull victims out of the wreckage.

question: A community health nurse wants to build strong herd immunity against a viral illness in a local village. What should be the top priority?

options.A: Distributing vitamin supplements

question: Why do PHC workers in rural areas often rely on basic tools and good clinical judgment?

options.A: Advanced medical equipment is rarely available at the grassroots level

options.C: Basic tools are proven to be more accurate than machines

question: Which of these is NOT a good quality for a clinical recommendation based on research data?

options.A: Being directly supported by the findings of the study
options.B: Being clear and easy for frontline nurses to understand
options.C: Being realistic about the equipment available in the clinic
options.D: Being completely unrealistic and impossible for staff to carry out

question: Why were early almshouses poorly suited for caring for the sick and elderly?

options.A: They suffered from severe overcrowding and a lack of medical staff
options.B: They charged fees that only wealthy families could afford
options.C: They focused too heavily on expensive experimental therapies

question: What is the main root cause behind gender-based violence?

options.A: Genetics and hereditary health disorders
options.B: Temporary financial stress in families
options.C: Lack of formal education in victims
options.D: Unequal power dynamics between genders

question: Where are the intercostal nerves located?

options.A: Deep in the neck muscles

question: What is the main result when a genetic mutation affects a receptor?

question: Why must a nurse check thyroid levels and ask about substance use when assessing a patient for anxiety?

options.A: Substance use screens are legally required for every psychiatric admission.

question: Why is the shift from paper charts to digital systems important for nurses?

options.A: It helps track patient trends and reduce errors
options.B: It slows down how quickly doctors can write new prescriptions
options.C: It removes all responsibility for charting from the nurse
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for direct patient contact

question: Into what smaller forms must dietary proteins be broken down before they can be absorbed?

options.A: Complex polysaccharides

options.D: Whole polypeptide chains

explanation: Proteins are usually too bulky to pass through the gut wall as they are, so digestive enzymes break them down into tiny building blocks like amino acids first.

question: What is the main cause of drug resistance in patients taking HIV treatment?

options.A: Inconsistent medication adherence allowing viral replication during low drug levels
options.B: Eating heavy fatty meals right before taking the evening dose
options.C: Swallowing pills with cold water instead of warm water
options.D: Storing medication bottles in brightly lit hospital rooms

question: What is the meeting point between the ectocervix and the endocervical canal called?

options.A: The myometrial junction

options.D: The pelvic floor arch

explanation: Spot on! It's called the transformation zone—a busy area where different types of cells meet and undergo active changes.

question: What is the main job of the myelin covering wrapped around a nerve fiber?

options.A: To manufacture neurotransmitters for the synapse
options.B: To anchor the neuron firmly to surrounding bone
options.C: To increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction
options.D: To provide a steady supply of oxygen to the neuron

explanation: Well done! Myelin acts like plastic insulation on an electrical wire, helping nerve signals travel much faster.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a microvascular complication of diabetes?

options.A: Peripheral stroke
options.B: Carotid atherosclerosis

options.D: Coronary artery disease

explanation: Retinopathy targets the tiny capillaries inside the eyes, making it a classic microvascular ('small vessel') complication.

question: How does the hypothalamus talk directly to the anterior pituitary gland?

options.A: By sending electrical nerve impulses across a large fluid gap

options.D: Through a specialized system of blood vessels called the portal system

question: Before giving an antibiotic, a nurse scans the patient's wristband and the drug barcode with a handheld scanner. What is this safety step called?

options.A: SBAR handoff reporting
options.B: Peer review auditing
options.C: Barcode medication administration
options.D: Root cause analysis

question: What do we call the emotional exhaustion nurses feel from constantly witnessing trauma and suffering in others?

options.A: Sensory overload
options.B: Innate immunity
options.C: Physical hypotension
options.D: Compassion fatigue

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard piece of guidance a nurse should give to promote healthy circulation in a pregnant woman?

options.A: Avoid standing motionless in one spot for long periods of time

options.C: Sleep on your side to prevent compression of major blood vessels

question: Why do leprosy patients often end up with serious sores on their hands and feet?

options.A: Unbearable itching makes them scratch too hard
options.B: Blood completely stops flowing to the fingers and toes
options.C: Loss of feeling causes them to injure themselves without knowing
options.D: Bacteria directly dissolve the skin cells

explanation: Because they can't feel pain, heat, or sharp objects, minor cuts go unnoticed and turn into nasty ulcers. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: When you add up all the percentages in a pie chart, what must they always equal?

options.A: The median value of the data
options.B: A maximum of 360 degrees
options.C: The total number of patients
options.D: Exactly 100 percent

explanation: Great job! Because a pie chart shows a complete whole, all the slices added together must always make 100 percent.

question: What actually happens to the prostate gland in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)?

options.A: Non-cancerous cell overgrowth
options.B: Infection-driven tissue necrosis
options.C: Malignant tumor invasion
options.D: Fibrotic tissue shrinking

question: Why does an injured area of the body become swollen, red, and warm?

options.A: Antibodies are tickling local nerve endings
options.B: Extra blood and fluid leak from widened blood vessels into the tissue
options.C: Cold blood gets trapped inside the injury

explanation: More blood rushes to the injury to help heal it, and fluid leaks out into the tissues, causing that familiar swelling and warmth.

question: Which clinical situation typically requires the administration of emergency and critical care drugs?

options.A: Discharge planning for a patient with a healed fracture
options.B: Annual physical checkup in a healthy adult client
options.C: A sudden, life-threatening crisis like cardiac arrest
options.D: Routine outpatient follow-up for chronic mild headache

explanation: Emergency drugs are reserved for critical, unstable situations where rapid intervention is necessary to save a life. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h6)

question: When is ibuprofen unsafe to use for fever in a child?

options.A: When the child is over one year of age
options.B: When the fever is lower than 38 degrees Celsius
options.C: When the child has concurrent dehydration or kidney issues
options.D: When the child has a mild ear infection

question: What part of a sterile field package is always considered contaminated?

options.A: The exact center of the drape
options.B: The items placed inside the wrapper
options.C: The outer one-inch border
options.D: The bottom surface resting on the table

question: Why are hypertension and dyslipidemia frequently referred to as silent conditions?

options.A: They disappear completely on their own without treatment
options.B: They rarely cause noticeable symptoms until severe damage occurs
options.C: They only occur in patients who cannot speak
options.D: They cannot be detected using standard medical equipment

explanation: High blood pressure and high cholesterol develop gradually over years without outward warning signs, making regular screening mandatory. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h6)

question: What is the main job of resuscitative equipment in the ward?

options.A: To provide routine daily patient hygiene care
options.B: To monitor long-term chronic wound healing
options.C: To manage sudden cardiac or respiratory arrest
options.D: To deliver oral medications during meals

explanation: You've got this! Resuscitative tools are kept ready specifically for emergencies when a patient stops breathing or their heart stops. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the very first thing you must do when starting a counselling session with a patient?

options.A: Building rapport and trust
options.B: Evaluating the final outcome
options.C: Setting strict behavioral rules
options.D: Discharging the patient

explanation: Before any healing conversation can happen, the patient needs to feel safe and welcome with you. Rapport is key!

question: What is the main thing that sets a medical emergency apart from a trauma case?

options.A: It is always caused by a blunt or penetrating external force
options.B: It occurs exclusively in patients with a history of surgery
options.C: It develops slowly over several months without sudden changes
options.D: It arises from internal disease processes or system breakdown

question: What does process data measure in a quality improvement project?

options.A: Patient satisfaction ratings collected after outpatient visits
options.B: The final health status of a patient after discharge
options.C: The total financial budget allocated to a specific ward
options.D: How healthcare services and nursing tasks are delivered

explanation: Process data is all about the *actions* we take. It checks if our day-to-day nursing tasks and clinical steps are actually being done.

question: A community nurse teaches schoolgirls how to maintain personal hygiene during menstruation. What is the main goal here?

options.A: To test the students on complex biological terminology

options.C: To build self-reliance and prevent preventable reproductive infections

question: Why should you sort waste right at the bedside or where it is generated?

options.A: To speed up the physical transport of bins to the incinerator

options.C: To reduce the number of waste bins needed in each ward
options.D: To make it easier for patients to clean up their bedside

explanation: Sorting waste immediately stops dangerous items from mixing with safe rubbish. It keeps disposal safe and easy for everyone!

question: Which color of blood collection tube is normally used for a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Red-top tube
options.B: Lavender-top tube
options.C: Gray-top tube
options.D: Light blue-top tube

explanation: Easy to remember in the ward! Gray-top tubes are your go-to tubes for blood sugar and glucose tolerance tests.

question: A patient in a rural Nigerian community comes in with a persistent fever in an area where malaria happens all year round. How would you classify this disease pattern?

options.A: Non-communicable illness
options.B: Endemic disease
options.C: Idiopathic condition
options.D: Pandemic outbreak

explanation: Since malaria is constantly present at a steady, predictable level in that community, it is classified as endemic.

question: Why is a biopsy a must-have test when checking for cancer?

options.A: It replaces the need for laboratory blood testing entirely.
options.B: It lowers systemic blood pressure during diagnostic scans.
options.C: It completely cures the patient by removing all toxins.
options.D: It provides definitive microscopic proof of malignancy.

explanation: Looking at actual cells under a microscope is the only way to be 100% sure whether cancer cells are present.

question: How can a growing economy help reduce the 'brain drain' of health professionals leaving Nigeria?

options.A: By providing competitive salaries and better working conditions locally
options.B: By making international travel passports illegal for nurses
options.C: By offering free housing in exchange for mandatory overtime
options.D: By forcing foreign hospitals to reject Nigerian applicants

explanation: If local pay and working conditions improve at home, nurses won't feel forced to look abroad for greener pastures.

question: What is the biggest clue in a patient's history that points to a future preterm birth?

options.A: A history of mild gestational diabetes
options.B: Gaining excessive weight during pregnancy
options.C: A history of a previous preterm birth
options.D: Maternal age under twenty years old

explanation: History is a powerful teacher! A mother who has delivered early before carries the highest risk of it happening again. You are building brilliant clinical instincts.

question: What happens to a hospital's safety culture when management ignores staff reports and refuses to fix staff shortages?

options.A: Nurses become more efficient and independent
options.B: The safety culture erodes and trust breaks down
options.C: Staff morale improves and errors decrease
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores increase rapidly

explanation: When leaders turn a blind eye to feedback, nurses stop reporting issues, and trust between the staff and management quickly falls apart.

question: What is the primary focus of the study of anatomy?

options.A: The electrical signals traveling through nerves
options.B: The physical structures and shapes of body parts
options.C: The chemical reactions inside living cells
options.D: The ways organs change when a person has a disease

explanation: Anatomy specifically looks at the physical structures, forms, and relative positions of body parts rather than how they function. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: A disaster survivor visits the clinic three months after a flood complaining of sudden nightmares, severe jumpiness, and avoiding the riverbank entirely. What condition is most likely?

options.A: Normal adjustment reaction
options.B: Bipolar manic episode
options.C: Acute Stress Disorder
options.D: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder

explanation: Flashbacks, avoidance, and hyperarousal lasting months after the traumatic event point directly toward PTSD. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is the main goal when medical help arrives immediately after a disaster?

options.A: To minimize death and illness
options.B: To train local volunteers
options.C: To rebuild damaged hospitals
options.D: To document insurance claims

explanation: You've got this! When disaster strikes, the immediate focus is always on saving lives and stopping severe illness through quick medical action.

question: What laboratory check is needed to tell Taenia saginata and Taenia solium apart with certainty?

options.A: Performing a chest X-ray to check for lung consolidation
options.B: Checking serum electrolyte levels for chronic dehydration
options.C: Examining the uterine branches of intact passed proglottids
options.D: Measuring total white blood cell counts in a routine blood sample

explanation: You got it! Lab techs count the side branches in the uterus of an intact passed segment to easily tell the two species apart.

question: Which body is officially responsible for regulating HMOs in Nigeria?

options.A: National Health Insurance Authority
options.B: Pharmaceutical Council of Nigeria
options.C: Nigerian Medical Association
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NHIA is the federal agency tasked with setting standards, registering, and monitoring all HMOs operating within the country. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h3)

question: What are the three main categories of immune system dysregulation?

options.A: Phagocytosis, inflammation, and complement activation
options.B: Hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, and immunodeficiency
options.C: Anaphylaxis, thrombosis, and necrosis
options.D: Antibody production, cellular immunity, and innate defense

explanation: Immune system dysregulation broadly breaks down into overreaction, attacking self-tissues, and underperformance. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h1)

question: What does open disclosure involve following a medical error?

options.A: Communicating transparently and empathetically with the patient and family about what happened
options.B: Sending a written letter through the mail without offering a meeting
options.C: Blaming the pharmacy department publicly during morning ward rounds
options.D: Hiding the mistake from the family until legal counsel advises otherwise

explanation: Open disclosure means being honest, clear, and empathetic with patients and families when medical errors occur. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h5)

question: A patient sends a photo of a swollen foot via WhatsApp for a nurse to check later. What type of communication is this?

options.A: Asynchronous delivery
options.B: Synchronous delivery
options.C: Direct ward admission
options.D: Emergency triage

explanation: Exactly! When you send a message or photo to be reviewed later without a live conversation happening right then, it is called asynchronous (or store-and-forward) communication.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major social determinant of health in Nigeria?

options.A: Availability of clean water and rural infrastructure
options.B: The brand of stethoscope used by attending physicians
options.C: Maternal education and literacy rates
options.D: Household income and overall poverty levels

explanation: Medical equipment brand does not determine public health outcomes, whereas income, education, and water supply profoundly affect community well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why does the World Health Organization (WHO) classify FGM into different types?

options.A: To determine how much financial compensation the family receives
options.B: To predict exactly how many children a woman can safely deliver
options.C: To measure the exact extent of tissue removal and anatomical alteration
options.D: To decide which surgical instruments should be sterilized

explanation: Having a clear classification system helps us document injuries accurately so we can give each patient the right, tailored care.

question: A patient taking a new antiarrhythmic drug tells the nurse they feel dizzy and lightheaded. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to stand up quickly to test their balance
options.B: Administer a dose of sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain
options.C: Check the patient's current blood pressure and heart rate
options.D: Hold the next scheduled dose and discharge the patient home

explanation: Dizziness and lightheadedness can signal a sudden drop in blood pressure or a slow heart rate caused by the drug. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h8)

question: How should a healthcare team view a patient who relapses after months of being sober?

options.A: As a signal to review and adjust the treatment plan rather than a total failure
options.B: As an intentional crime that requires immediate notification of law enforcement
options.C: As an expected physical cure that means treatment is permanently finished
options.D: As definitive proof that the person is hopeless and should be abandoned

explanation: Just like managing hypertension or diabetes, a setback in a chronic condition means we tweak our approach, not give up on the patient!

question: Why do market porters who carry heavy loads on their heads often suffer from chronic back and neck pain?

options.A: They suffer from acute biological infections spread by insects
options.B: They experience psychosocial stress from working long hours
options.C: They are exposed to dangerous chemical solvents in the market
options.D: They face severe ergonomic strain from heavy lifting and poor posture

explanation: Balancing heavy loads incorrectly puts immense pressure on the spine and supporting muscles, leading to long-term pain.

question: A nurse notices a stroke patient suddenly loses the ability to speak clearly and starts mixing up words. Which assessment priority is most urgent?

options.A: Inspecting the patient's skin for pressure ulcers
options.B: Checking the patient's hearing with a tuning fork
options.C: Evaluating language and speech areas in the brain
options.D: Testing lower leg reflexes with a percussion hammer

explanation: Sudden speech changes point to acute involvement of language centers like Broca's or Wernicke's areas, demanding prompt neurological tracking. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h7)

question: How should a nurse respond when a teen shares a wild cultural myth about birth control?

options.A: Laugh to show how ridiculous the rumor sounds to professionals
options.B: Scold the teenager for believing such foolish stories in public
options.C: Gently validate their concern and provide accurate, simple facts
options.D: Ignore the statement entirely and prescribe whatever is easiest

explanation: Always meet patients with kindness, not judgment. Listening first helps you correct misinformation effectively.

question: What is the main difference between a reservoir and a source of infection?

options.A: A reservoir is always a non-living object, while a source is always an animal
options.B: A reservoir only contains viruses, whereas a source only contains bacteria
options.C: A reservoir causes mild symptoms, but a source causes deadly disease outbreaks
options.D: A reservoir is where the germ naturally lives, while a source is where you catch it from

explanation: You've got this! The reservoir is the germ's long-term home base, while the source is the immediate spot or item that passes it to you.

question: Why don't modern hospitals just use simple boiling water to process surgical instruments?

options.A: It leaves a toxic chemical residue on the metal surface
options.B: It melts stainless steel components and plastic handles
options.C: It fails to reliably destroy bacterial endospores
options.D: It takes significantly longer than standard steam autoclaves

explanation: Boiling water is great for killing regular bacteria, but some hardy spores can survive 100°C. That's why we rely on autoclaves instead!

question: After dietary fats are repackaged into chylomicrons, which system do they enter first?

options.A: The pulmonary circulation
options.B: The portal venous system
options.C: The lymphatic system
options.D: The systemic arterial tree

explanation: That's right! Because chylomicrons are too bulky for regular blood capillaries, they sneak into tiny lymphatic vessels called lacteals inside the villi first.

question: How do rigid hierarchies in some healthcare settings hurt patient safety?

options.A: Patients receive conflicting instructions from different specialists
options.B: Junior nurses may be afraid to speak up or question unsafe orders from senior staff
options.C: Hospital management is unable to purchase necessary medications
options.D: Doctors are forced to perform routine nursing documentation tasks

explanation: Fear of senior staff can keep junior nurses quiet about dangerous orders. Open teamwork saves lives!

question: What is the most common underlying cause of postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Retained placenta
options.B: Coagulation failure
options.C: Uterine atony
options.D: Vaginal tearing

explanation: Uterine atony happens when the muscle of the uterus fails to contract properly after delivery, leaving open blood vessels that bleed heavily. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h2)

question: What is the term for a resting heart rate that drops below 60 beats per minute?

options.A: Tachypnea
options.B: Bradycardia
options.C: Hypotension
options.D: Tachycardia

explanation: Bradycardia simply means a slow heart rate (under 60 bpm in adults). You are building a strong clinical vocabulary! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: Why is being kind and compassionate so important when caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: It prevents the physical pain caused by uterine contractions
options.B: It shortens the standard hospital stay to less than two hours
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any antibiotic therapy
options.D: It reduces anxiety and encourages honest disclosure of medical history

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from judgment, they are much more likely to share true details that help us care for them better.

question: A client with severe hypertension asks for oral contraceptive pills. What should the nurse do during the assessment?

options.A: Identify hypertension as a contraindication and discuss safer alternative methods
options.B: Prescribe the pills immediately because blood pressure does not matter
options.C: Refuse to check the client's blood pressure during the visit
options.D: Tell the client that birth control pills cure high blood pressure

explanation: Estrogen-containing pills can worsen high blood pressure and increase stroke risk, so nurses must screen for medical conditions and offer safer choices like progestin-only options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: What is the major danger of giving a purgative to a patient with a bowel obstruction?

options.A: It will immediately cure the blockage
options.B: It can cause the bowel to rupture
options.C: It causes severe high blood pressure
options.D: It turns the stool completely black

explanation: Watch out for this! Forcing muscle contractions against a blocked pathway raises pressure dangerously and can tear the bowel wall.

question: What does a negative correlation mean between two variables?

options.A: Both variables decrease at the exact same time.
options.B: There is no relationship whatsoever between the variables.
options.C: The data collected by the researcher is invalid.
options.D: As one variable increases, the other variable decreases.

explanation: You're doing great! Think of it like a seesaw: when one thing goes up (like daily exercise), the other thing goes down (like resting blood pressure). That is a negative correlation!

question: Why do different agencies need to work together during a disaster response?

options.A: It gives nurses the authority to write new national laws
options.B: It replaces the need for community education and local drills
options.C: It guarantees that natural hazards will completely miss the country
options.D: It ensures that different groups do not duplicate efforts and waste resources

explanation: Brilliant! Sharing information and working hand-in-hand prevents confusion and keeps help running smoothly.

question: Why is 'operational scalability' so important for a Rapid Response Center?

options.A: It allows the center to expand or shrink its response as the emergency changes
options.B: It prevents staff members from ever working overtime shifts
options.C: It ensures that all patients receive identical care regardless of injury severity
options.D: It guarantees that funding will never run out during a crisis

explanation: Emergencies change fast. Scalability means the center can ramp up gear and staff when things get worse, or scale down safely when things calm down.

question: What is a major advantage of cross-sectional research?

options.A: It requires zero participation from human subjects
options.B: It is relatively quick and cost-effective to conduct
options.C: It proves the exact cause of chronic diseases over time
options.D: It eliminates all forms of human bias automatically

explanation: No need to wait years! Cross-sectional studies save precious time and money because everything happens in one go.

question: A nurse identifies a case of polio. Why do we place polio in a special, urgent reporting category?

options.A: It is a targeted disease for global eradication and elimination
options.B: It only affects elderly patients in urban hospitals
options.C: It is a common seasonal allergy with mild symptoms
options.D: It does not require tracking by government agencies

explanation: The world is actively trying to wipe out polio completely. Because every single case is a global emergency, we track them with extreme urgency!

question: A patient gets a painful, pus-filled swelling where they received an injection days ago. What happened?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the cotton wool used afterward
options.B: A normal immune response to the medication formula
options.C: A localized bacterial infection introduced during the procedure
options.D: Systemic failure of the patient's cardiovascular system

explanation: When hygiene slips, bacteria can hitch a ride on the needle and cause a painful abscess right in the tissue.

question: In secretory diarrhoea, why do patients lose water so quickly?

options.A: The liver fails to produce bile acids for digestion
options.B: Intestinal cells actively pump excessive water into the gut lumen
options.C: Stomach acid production increases to dangerous levels
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering waste products completely

explanation: Think of it like an open tap! Toxins trick the cells in the intestines into pushing out lots of water and salt into the gut faster than the body can absorb it.

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: To restrict patient access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: To eliminate the need for clinical supervision in rural clinics
options.C: To track service quality, identify gaps, and guide continuous improvement
options.D: To punish nurses who make minor documentation errors in patient charts

explanation: You're doing great! Monitoring collects essential data so managers can improve care delivery and patient safety.

question: Which oral antifungal drug is a favorite for treating urinary yeast infections because it travels well into the urine?

options.A: Clotrimazole
options.B: Fluconazole
options.C: Ketoconazole
options.D: Miconazole

explanation: Fluconazole is easily absorbed and concentrates nicely right where it's needed in the urinary tract. Great choice for a quick pill!
